$comment: SHARED ERROR MESSAGE CATALOGUE — the contract between the Strapi seed and the
C# compiled fallback for the citizen-facing text of every stable error keyword.
The live catalogue is the `error-message` collection in MyssContent (Strapi).
A Service Designer edits a row there and publishes; the new wording is served
without a deploy. This file seeds that collection on a fresh database AND is
the text MyssApi serves when Strapi cannot be read, so it is mirrored twice:
Apps/MyssContent/src/lib/error-message-seed-data.ts   (the seed)
Apps/MyssApi/Data/ErrorMessageDefaults.cs             (the compiled fallback)
Both are tested against this file, so a divergence is a failing test rather
than two systems quietly wording the same failure differently.
The seed is create-if-missing: a row the designer has already edited in the
admin panel is never overwritten by a restart. Changing the text here changes
the fallback and what a fresh environment starts with, not a live row.
RULES FOR EDITING
- A keyword is DOMAIN.CONTEXT.NAME in upper case, and is never reused for a
different meaning. Adding one means adding it to both mirrors.
- Only keywords whose wording is the same wherever they are raised belong
here. FORM.FIELD.REQUIRED is deliberately absent: its wording is authored
per field on the form (errors.required / validate.customMessage), and the
bus pass rules carry field-specific wording of their own.
- Keywords whose message embeds a value stay in code until the resolver
supports placeholders: FORM.FIELD.UNKNOWN and FORM.FIELD.WRONG_TYPE name
the key, FORM.VERSION.UNKNOWN names the version. BUSPASS.SUBMIT.ICM_UNAVAILABLE
is worded by the browser from the API's verdict on whether the ministry may
already hold the request, so one keyword has two texts and stays there too.
- `note` says where the keyword is raised, for the designer's benefit. It is
seeded into the row but never shown to a citizen.
